The time-space optimized learned index ALEX exhibits critical vulnerabilities, with its structure prone to collapse under both duplicated-key and dense-key attacks, which are common operational scenarios. This reveals the urgent need to design learned indexes that achieve both time-space efficiency and structural robustness. 3 The LIFT Index Framework Based on the observations in Section 2, we design an updatable time-space tradeoff learned index, LIFT. In Section 3.1, we present the overall structure and basic operations of LIFT. Section 3.2 discusses the concurrent implementation of LIFT. Section 3.3 addresses the defense structure in LIFT against poisoning attacks. 3.1 The Overall Framework of LIFT Figure 3 illustrates the overall architecture of LIFT, which is primarily composed of inner nodes and leaf nodes. During the construction process, we introduce gaps into all nodes and employ a quantitative approach to ensure a balance between performance and space overhead, thereby achieving a time-space optimized index structure. Implementation details can be found in Section 4. Specifically, our proposed construction strategy ensures that query operations in inner nodes are fully accurate, with no prediction errors (see Section 4.3 for details). Each inner node stores pointers to the lower-level of inner or leaf nodes.
